purpose: Apply the standing rule that a live-node invocation found in successful historical evidence is reused byte-for-byte, while never inventing provenance for commands that have not passed live.
audit_scope: pilot_rows network-release and aggregate-presence node commands

node_local_input_stage.finding: Attempts 1 through 15 contain no non-rehearsal PASS_NODE_LOCAL_INPUT_STAGE receipt.
node_local_input_stage.successor_control: Persist a write-once canonical command-bundle hash before the first live SSM invocation and carry that hash into its stage receipt.

pilot_workload.finding: Attempts 1 through 15 contain no non-rehearsal PASS_PILOT_ROWS receipt.
pilot_workload.successor_control: Render the workload from one module constant, record the NUL-delimited container argv hash in qualification, and bind the rendered workload hash before first live execution.

other_eval_node_command_families.finding: No successful non-rehearsal eval stage receipt through attempt 15 proves these command families. Attempt 15 executed volume preparation, but its enclosing gpu_and_sampler_gate receipt is REFUSED and does not embed the command bytes, so it is not promoted to historical proof.
other_eval_node_command_families.successor_control: External-tool and SSM command IDs remain bounded and sanitized; the first successful live stage receipts must preserve their exact command-bundle identities before any later executor may cite them as proven.

deviations: The B6A receipt binds the successful script by path and SHA-256 rather than embedding the full command string. The executor therefore compares its canonical NUL-delimited argv bytes to the exact invocation extracted from the receipt-bound script; this is stronger than comparing to an unbound transcription.

Node-local staging and the pilot workload cannot be bound to successful historical receipts because no such receipts exist. They remain explicitly unproven and receive first-live command-identity receipts instead of fabricated provenance.
